docs.title: What is Java?
docs.text:
Java is a high-level, object-oriented, platform-independent programming language developed by Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle).

It is designed to be: - Simple - Secure - Robust - Portable

Java follows the principle: "Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA)"

docs.title: Why Learn Java?
docs.text:
Java is one of the most in-demand programming languages.

It is widely used in: - Web applications - Android mobile apps - Enterprise systems - Automation testing (Selenium, TestNG)

✔ Beginner-friendly ✔ Huge community support ✔ Used in real-world projects

docs.title: Platform Independent
docs.text: Java code can run on any system that has JVM installed.

docs.title: Object-Oriented
docs.text: Everything in Java is based on objects and classes.

docs.title: Secure
docs.text: Java does not use pointers and has built-in security features.

docs.title: Robust
docs.text: Strong memory management and exception handling.

docs.title: Multithreaded
docs.text: Java supports running multiple tasks at the same time.

docs.title: Java Architecture (VERY IMPORTANT)
docs.text: Java works using three main components:

docs.title: 1. JVM (Java Virtual Machine)
docs.text:
JVM is the engine that runs Java programs.

Responsibilities: - Executes bytecode - Converts bytecode into machine code - Manages memory - Handles garbage collection

✔ Platform dependent ✔ Core of Java runtime

docs.title: 2. JRE (Java Runtime Environment)
docs.text:
JRE provides the environment to run Java programs.

It includes: - JVM - Libraries - Runtime files

✔ Used only for running Java programs

docs.title: 3. JDK (Java Development Kit)
docs.text:
JDK is used for developing Java applications.

It includes: - JRE - Compiler (javac) - Tools (debugger, etc.)

✔ Used for writing + compiling + running

docs.title: Relationship
docs.text:
JDK = JRE + Development Tools
JRE = JVM + Libraries

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
In this chapter, you will learn:

  • What is JDK
  • How to install Java
  • How to set environment variables
  • How to verify installation

docs.title: What is JDK?
docs.text:
JDK (Java Development Kit) is required to:

  • Write Java programs
  • Compile code
  • Run applications

It includes: - JRE (Java Runtime Environment) - JVM (Java Virtual Machine)

docs.title: Step 1: Download Java (JDK)
docs.text:
1. Go to the official website: https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/

  2. Choose:

  3. Latest LTS version (Recommended)

  4. Windows / Mac / Linux (based on your system)

  5. Download the installer

docs.title: For Windows:
docs.text:
1. Double-click the downloaded .exe file
  2. Click Next
  3. Choose install location (default is fine)
  4. Click Install
  5. Finish installation

docs.title: For Mac:
docs.text:
1. Open .dmg file
  2. Follow installation steps
  3. Complete setup

docs.title: Why Needed?
docs.text: To run Java from anywhere in command prompt

docs.title: Steps:
docs.text:
1. Open Start Menu
  2. Search: Environment Variables
  3. Click: Edit the system environment variables
  4. Click: Environment Variables

docs.title: Add JAVA_HOME
docs.text:
1. Click New under System Variables
  2. Add:
Variable Name: JAVA_HOME
Variable Value: C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-XX

Replace XX with your version

docs.title: Update Path
docs.text:
1. Select Path → Click Edit
  2. Click New

  3. Add: text %JAVA_HOME%\bin

  4. Click OK

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Open Command Prompt and type:

java -version

docs.text: Keyword Purpose Example public Access modifier (visible everywhere) public class class Defines a class class MyClass static Belongs to class (not object) static void main void No return value void main() int Integer data type int age = 25; String Text data type String name = "John"; main Entry point method main(String[] args) System Built-in class System.out out Output stream out.println() println Print with newline println("Hello")

docs.title: Step 2: Complete Hello World Program
docs.text:
public class Hello {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello World!");
        System.out.println("My First Java Program");
    }
}

docs.title: Step 3: Compile & Run (Command Prompt)
docs.text:
# Navigate to folder containing Hello.java
cd C:\JavaPractice

# Compile (creates Hello.class)
javac Hello.java

# Run
java Hello

Output:

Hello World!
My First Java Program

docs.title: Syntax Rules (Detailed)
docs.text:
// 1. EVERY statement ends with ;
int x = 10;        //  Correct
int y = 20         //  Error!

// 2. Braces ALWAYS match
public class Test {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello");  //  Braces match
    }  // ← Closing brace required
}    // ← Class closing brace

// 3. main() method REQUIRED (exact signature)
public static void main(String[] args)  //  Correct
public static void Main(String args)    //  Wrong case
static void main(String[] args)         //  Missing public

docs.title: Syntax Checklist
docs.text:
File name = Class name (.java)
public class ClassName
public static void main(String[] args)
Every statement ends with ;
Braces match {} for class & main
Semicolons after variables
No spaces in keywords

docs.title: Quick Test
docs.text:
Does this compile?

public class Test {
    public static void main(String[] args)
    {
        System.out.println("Test");
    }
}

Answer: NO (missing { after main())
